content:
General Motors first announced back in 2023 that it would abandon CarPlay across all of its future electric vehicles, and subsequently came up with a string of absurd excuses, at one point even hinting that this was something Steve Jobs would have done.

But it seems there is now an exception. Since that policy reversal was reportedly driven by customer feedback, perhaps GM is now revisiting its major decision…

Engadget was first to report on the CarBuzz story.

The Cadillac online configurator already has a few 2027 models up, and we noticed that the Lyriq still comes standard with CarPlay and Android Auto. The Lyriq is Cadillac's first all-electric vehicle, and is also a tech-leading model that we believe is steadily becoming one of the best luxury EVs out there. A Cadillac spokesperson told CarBuzz: "Based on customer feedback, Cadillac is continually refining its infotainment strategy for its EV portfolio while prioritising in-vehicle native experiences."

Put simply: we've found that customers won't buy a luxury EV without CarPlay.

Engadget also pointed out a handy alternative for owners of other GM vehicles that lack CarPlay.

Could this be the beginning of the end of GM's CarPlay divorce? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
